title: A uniform respiration step needs at least 7.24 umol/kg error in five North Pacific oxygen records
abstract: Can one uniform respiration increase explain the North Pacific oxygen histories under fixed transport? We allow any nonnegative transit-age distribution in each of five regions and test published sigma0 26.5 ship oxygen estimates in 1984-2025. Every model needs at least 7.243 umol/kg error in one five-year block mean. A transition-zone convexity inequality proves this bound for all real step dates and unbounded age support. A common-rate model reaches the bound, so it is sharp for the permitted family. The shared-rate and reference-AOU constraints do not raise the primary bound. Omitting the transition zone reduces the numerical bound to 5.208; annual data need 14.217. This extends the earlier result that respiration can produce later decline midpoints in older water. Full histories supply a stronger test than midpoint order. The tolerance is deterministic, not a statistical rejection. Sparse cruises, correlated annual errors and temporal averaging limit inference. General changing respiration, variable transport and independent tracer constraints are outside scope. Code, frozen aggregate inputs, primal and dual solutions, a separate proof audit and reproduction instructions are included.

display.caption: Observed regional block means, unrestricted age-response fits, and required error by step year. Error tolerances are not confidence limits.

citations.reason: Frozen regional ship oxygen series and reference AOU. We test the full-history respiration alternative to its midpoint argument.
Respiration exposure formula and timing counterexample. We extend the test to arbitrary age distributions and full regional histories.
